title: Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts Cancelled With the Vehicle Kept — Refund and Acceptance
content:
## Scope
This Kessler Shield Vehicle Service Contracts rule applies to a contract its holder cancels while keeping the vehicle. The signed cancellation request must give the holder's own request as the reason; such a cancellation is a kept-vehicle cancellation. The rule applies only to such a cancellation.

When the holder accepts the cancellation:
- the request is completed;
- the contract moves to cancelled, effective on the request date;
- the refund is recorded as due on that date, at the odometer certified on the request, under the refund basis that applies.

## When the refund is fixed
The refund on such a cancellation is fixed only after the contract's latest component repair line denied for the waiting period (by decision date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history) has been re-decided and whatever that re-decision owes the holder has been paid, wherever that line was denied while the contract was sold on its vehicle's purchase deal, its component group is not an internally lubricated one (engine, transmission or drive axle) and has its coverage switch true, the repair order's diagnosis date and the line's odometer fall within the term, and that repair order carries a diagnostic fee on exactly one concern line together with the store's customer-pay labor on that concern line, not wholly credited back as a comeback repair, closed on or after the day the line was decided.

The refund on such a cancellation is not computed until the rental benefit of the claim of the contract's latest component-repair line, paid or denied (by entry date; on a same-day tie, the one that appears first in the claim history), has been settled and whatever rental it owes the holder has been paid, wherever the first loaner agreement the loaner records list for that claim's repair order is a Kessler loaner on which the holder was charged daily rental and the coverage level's rental amount per day and rental day limit are both above zero.

## Acceptance tool: `accept_kept_vehicle_cancellation_d270783c`
**Owner.** This is the holder's own action. The agent unlocks `accept_kept_vehicle_cancellation_d270783c` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to accept the cancellation quote.

**Effects of one run.**
- The signed cancellation request on file is marked completed.
- The contract moves to cancelled, with the effective date as its closed date.
- One refund calculation entry is booked on the contract, dated the effective date, with the certified odometer, the refund basis and the refund amount.
- The contract's refund-due balance rises by that amount.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `vsc_contract_id` | the record identifier of the contract being cancelled, as returned by the service contract lookup and read to the holder by the desk | Id |
| `vsc_cancel_request_id` | the identifier of the holder's signed cancellation request on file for this contract, as returned by the cancellation request lookup and read to the holder by the desk | Id |
| `effective_date` | the effective cancellation date | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `odometer_at_request` | the odometer certified on the cancellation request | whole miles, no separators |
| `cancel_method` | the basis of the refund | `flat_free_look` (full price refunded inside the free look), `flat_deal_unwound` (full price refunded because the purchase deal was unwound) or `pro_rata` (the unused share of the price); `not_applicable` is listed but not accepted (it marks claim entries only) |
| `refund_amount` | the refund the holder accepts | USD with 2 decimal places, half up to the cent, 0.00 or more |

**Return.** A confirmation naming the refund calculation reference (an opaque id), the cancelled contract, the effective date and the refund amount, with 2 decimal places. Its presence means the request was completed, the contract is cancelled and the refund is recorded as due. Any of the following returns an error, and nothing is booked:
- a refund amount below 0.00;
- an odometer that is not whole miles;
- a refund basis outside the three listed;
- an effective date not written YYYY-MM-DD.
